title: A / an, the and zero article 2
subtitle: a journalist / (the) head of the company
summary: Use articles correctly with jobs, people's names and superlatives, and use this the way speakers do when they start a story.

lesson.heading: A job or a job title?

left.label: a / an - what a person's job is
examples: She was **a company director** when she retired.
Against her parents' wishes, she wants to be **a journalist**.
I'm **a production manager** at Fino. (= there may be more than one production manager)

right.label: the or zero article - a job title or a unique position
examples: She's been appointed **(the) head** of the company.
Dr Simons has taken on the position of **Head of Department**.

lesson.note: After the position of, the post of or the role of we always use zero article before the job title.

lesson.heading: the before a person's name
lesson.text: We usually use **zero article** before the name of an individual person or place. But we use **the** to specify which of two people with the same name we mean, to mark out the most famous person with that name (here *the* is stressed), with an adjective or a job noun, and when we talk about a family as a whole.

examples.text: That's not **the** Stephen Fraser I went to school with.
examples.note: compare There was a Stephen Fraser in my class. = a person named Stephen Fraser

examples.text: Do they mean **the** Neil Armstrong, or someone else?
**the** late Michael Jackson; **(the)** artist Joseph Turner
examples.note: the is sometimes left out, particularly in journalism

lesson.heading: a / an before a name
lesson.text: **A / an** (or sometimes zero article) is used with a name to refer to the particular excellent qualities of the person named, and for an individual example of a product or a work by a particular artist. We also use *a / an* before a person's name if we don't know the person ourselves.

examples.text: Majid plays tennis well, but he'll never be **(a)** Roger Federer.
I've just bought **a** Mercedes. Do you think it could be **a** Van Gogh?
Dr Lee is here for you.
There's **a** Dr Amy Lee on the phone. Do you want to talk to her?
examples.note: = I haven't heard of her before

lesson.heading: this in stories and jokes
lesson.text: In stories and jokes in conversation, **this** is commonly used instead of *a / an* to introduce a new person or thing. Using *this* highlights that person or thing as the topic of what is to come next.

examples.text: As I was walking along, **this spider** landed on my head, and ...
**This man** goes into a chemist and he says ...

lesson.heading: the with superlatives

left.label: the is needed - a noun or defining phrase follows
examples: He is **the finest young player** around at the moment.
It was **the cheapest** I could find.
The Pacific is **the biggest ocean** in the world.

right.label: the can be left out - nothing follows
examples: *A:* Why did you decide to stay in this hotel? *B:* It was **(the) cheapest**.
*A:* Why did you ask Martina to go first? *B:* Because she's **(the) oldest**.

lesson.note: Leaving out the is particularly common in an informal style.

lesson.text: *A / an* answers *what kind of person is she?*; *the* or no article answers *which post does she hold?* - so a production manager but (the) head of the company.

exercises.prompt: She was determined to be ___ one day.
exercises.explanation: We use a / an to say what a person's job is, was or will be.

exercises.prompt: A: What make is your computer? B: It's ___.
exercises.explanation: a / an is used for an individual example of a product made by a particular manufacturer.

exercises.statement: I didn't even know Clara was interested in art until I heard that she owns Van Gogh.
exercises.explanation: ... she owns a Van Gogh. We use a / an for a work by a particular artist.
We use the when we talk about a family as a whole.

exercises.prompt: I found myself talking to George Clooney! Not ___, of course, but someone with the same name.
exercises.explanation: Stressed the marks out the most famous person with that name.

exercises.statement: I've been offered the position of Director of Personnel.
exercises.explanation: Correct. After the position of we use zero article before the job title.
Before the name of an individual person we normally use zero article.

exercises.prompt: A doctor you have never heard of is on the phone for your colleague. Tell them.
exercises.answer: There's a Dr Amy Lee on the phone.
exercises.explanation: a / an before a person's name shows that you don't know the person yourself.

exercises.prompt: Something very strange happened to me the other night. As I was going home ___ came up to me.
exercises.explanation: In a story this often replaces a / an to introduce someone as the topic of what comes next.

exercises.prompt: He told me that he was ___ head of the local council and that he was offering me a job.
exercises.explanation: For a unique position we use the (or zero article), not a / an.

exercises.prompt: He's really keen on athletics. He likes to think of himself as ___.
exercises.explanation: a / an - or zero article - refers to the excellent qualities of the person named; the would mean the athlete himself.

exercises.prompt: In each sentence, must the stay or can it be left out?

items.text: It's ___ best ice-cream I've ever tasted.
Rodrigo's boat wasn't the most elegant in the harbour, but it was certainly ___ biggest.
I thought the second competitor was ___ best, even though he didn't win a prize.
This is by far ___ most valuable painting in the collection.
Why did you ask Martina to go first? Because she's ___ oldest.
Sapphires occur in a variety of colours, but blue ones are ___ most valuable.
The Pacific is ___ biggest ocean in the world.
It's supposed to be ___ oldest post office in the country.
